item.title: TT-104: Undo for TaskStore
item.brief:
Repository: long-backlog (contains the tasktracker package and BACKLOG.md). Implement ticket TT-104 from BACKLOG.md exactly, following its acceptance criteria.

TT-104: Undo.
`tasktracker.store.TaskStore` has `add`, `complete` and `delete`. Add `undo()`:
- It reverts the most recent not-yet-undone `add`, `complete` or `delete`; repeated calls walk further back (LIFO), across all three kinds.
- Undoing an `add` removes that task; undoing a `complete` makes the task open again; undoing a `delete` restores the task exactly as it was, under the same id.
- Ids are never reused, even after undoing an `add`.
- With nothing left to undo, `undo()` raises `NothingToUndo` (defined in `tasktracker.store`).
- Failed operations (e.g. completing an unknown id) are not recorded.

Constraints: standard library only. Keep the existing tests passing with `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t .`. Add unit tests for every behaviour above, including LIFO across mixed kinds, id non-reuse after undoing an add, and failed operations not being recorded. Commit only on this item's branch, as one commit, with a clear message. Do not push. Do not change files for other tickets (TT-101 to TT-103) beyond what this ticket needs. Do not ask questions; if something is ambiguous, pick the most literal reading of the ticket and state it in your summary.

item.title: TT-103: Search query syntax
item.brief:
Repository: long-backlog (contains the tasktracker package and BACKLOG.md). Implement ticket TT-103 from BACKLOG.md exactly, following its acceptance criteria.

TT-103: Search query syntax.
`tasktracker.search.search(tasks, query)` only does a case-sensitive substring match on titles. Support a small query language instead:
- The query is split into terms on whitespace, except inside double quotes: `"fix login"` is one phrase term. All terms must match (AND).
- A bare word or phrase matches when it appears in the title, case-insensitively.
- `tag:NAME` matches tasks that have the tag NAME (exact tag, case-insensitive).
- `status:open` / `status:done` match on status.
- Any other `field:value` term, an unknown status, or an unterminated quote raises `QueryError` (defined in `tasktracker.search`).
- An empty or blank query matches every task. Results keep the input order.

Constraints: standard library only. Keep the existing tests passing with `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t .`. Add unit tests for every behaviour above. Commit only on this item's branch, as one commit, with a clear message. Do not push. Do not change files for other tickets (TT-101, TT-102, TT-104) beyond what this ticket needs. Do not ask questions; if something is ambiguous, pick the most literal reading of the ticket and state it in your summary.

Unknown fields, unknown status, empty tag name and unterminated quotes raise QueryError (a ValueError subclass). Blank query matches all, input order kept. item.title: TT-102: RFC 4180 CSV export
item.brief:
Repository: long-backlog (contains the tasktracker package and BACKLOG.md). Implement ticket TT-102 from BACKLOG.md exactly, following its acceptance criteria.

TT-102: RFC 4180 CSV export.
`tasktracker.export.to_csv(tasks)` joins fields with commas and breaks on titles containing commas, quotes or newlines. It must produce RFC 4180 CSV:
- Header `id,title,tags,status,due`; one row per task in the given order.
- Tags joined with `;`, due date as ISO `YYYY-MM-DD` or empty.
- A field containing a comma, double quote, CR or LF is wrapped in double quotes, with embedded double quotes doubled. Other fields are not quoted.
- Every line (header included) ends with CRLF.

Constraints: standard library only. Keep the existing tests passing with `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t .`. Add unit tests for every behaviour above, including titles with commas, quotes, CR and LF, and tags/due edge cases. Commit only on this item's branch, as one commit, with a clear message. Do not push. Do not change files for other tickets (TT-101, TT-103, TT-104) beyond what this ticket needs. Do not ask questions; if something is ambiguous, pick the most literal reading of the ticket and state it in your summary.

item.title: TT-101: Reject impossible due dates in parse_due
item.brief:
Repository: long-backlog (contains the tasktracker package and BACKLOG.md). Implement ticket TT-101 from BACKLOG.md exactly, following its acceptance criteria.

TT-101: Reject impossible due dates.
`tasktracker.dates.parse_due(text, today)` silently clamps impossible dates: `2026-02-30` becomes `2026-02-28`. Instead:
- An impossible calendar date (`2026-02-30`, `2025-02-29`, `2026-04-31`, `2026-13-01`, `2026-00-10`) raises `InvalidDate`, a `ValueError` subclass defined in `tasktracker.dates`, whose message contains the original text.
- Anything else that does not match a supported form also raises `InvalidDate` (today it raises a bare `ValueError`).
- Relative offsets: `+Nd` is N days after `today`, `+0d` is `today`. Negative or unsigned offsets (`-3d`, `3d`) raise `InvalidDate`.
- `today` and `tomorrow` keep working; matching stays case-insensitive and ignores surrounding whitespace.

Constraints: standard library only. Keep the existing tests passing with `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t .`. Add unit tests for every behaviour above. Commit only on this item's branch, as one commit, with a clear message. Do not push. Do not change files for other tickets (TT-102 to TT-104) beyond what this ticket needs. Do not ask questions; if something is ambiguous, pick the most literal reading of the ticket and state it in your summary.
